subject: Tri-region activation checklist and SKU confirmation — HelixAI
messages:
From: Emma Clarke <emma@helixai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixai.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tri-region onboarding — initial numbers

Sergio — thanks for the walkthrough this morning. We reviewed the rough throughput numbers with our infra team and want to lock down a tentative node mix for the first 90 days so procurement can draft the purchase order. Key asks: 1) can you confirm per-region sustained QPS for the A100 vs H100 SKU mix (we care about token latency at 512 token context); 2) what burst cushion do you typically reserve for deal-led pools vs sustained capacity; and 3) any obvious compliance/residency caveats if we choose Frankfurt for EU and Singapore for APAC?

Attached a quick spreadsheet with our estimated traffic split and a draft SOW (HelixAI_SOW_v1.2.pdf). Happy to jump on a call but wanted to capture the asks in writing first.

—Emma
Head of Platform Eng, HelixAI
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@helixai.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tri-region onboarding — initial numbers

Emma — thanks, got the sheet and SOW. Quick answers up front, then I pulled in ops: 

- Sustained QPS guidance (512 ctx): US (west) — 220 QPS per H100 node, 130 QPS per A100s; EU (Frankfurt) — ~200 / 115; APAC (Singapore) — ~180 / 100. These are conservative sustained numbers assuming mixed batching and 95th P50 latency targets at ~120–200ms depending on request shape.

- Burst cushion: for deal-led Dedicated pools we recommend a 20–30% burst buffer (reserved burst nodes that can be hot-buffered). We can offer an initial 25% burst commitment on month 1 for HelixAI.

- Residency/compliance: Frankfurt meets EU data residency; Singapore requires confirming local logging retention policy — we'll need to map GDPR+PDPA controls to your SOW items (I copied Rachel for compliance alignment).

I'll summarize node SKU options in a follow-up mail and propose a delta SOW that encodes the burst cushion.

Action items: Rachel — can you validate the latency assumptions and add a short compliance checklist for Frankfurt/Singapore? Karthik — please run a quick cost delta for 25% burst across a 3-month ramp.

—Sergio
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Emma Clarke <emma@helixai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tri-region onboarding — initial numbers

Emma / team — quick compliance + perf notes: 

- Perf: Sergio's numbers look reasonable. For headroom-sensitive workloads (low-latency chat) recommend pinning the US pool to H100-heavy (70% H100 / 30% A100) to meet 100–150ms p95 for 512 ctx. EU and APAC can be more A100-weighted to save cost if latency tolerance is higher.

- Caching: we can enable prefix KV cache for common prompts which reduces sustained QPS by ~10–18% depending on hit rates — worth instrumenting in your eval set.

- Compliance checklist (high-level): 
  * Frankfurt: KMS-backed keys (customer-managed possible), audit logs retention policy 90 days by default (extendable), SOC2 Type II evidence available. 
  * Singapore: PDPA alignment required — confirm local legal on log retention; if you need on-prem/private deployment for APAC we can scope that but it'll change lead times and costs.

I'll attach a minimal checklist and a sample SLA addendum for Frankfurt. Laura — can you include this in the updated SOW revision?

—Rachel
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Clarke <emma@helixai.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tri-region onboarding — initial numbers (cost delta)

Team / Emma — I ran the cost delta in the attached SKU matrix (helix-node-sku-matrix.xlsx). Highlights: 

- Baseline (no burst): monthly committed spend estimate = $84.2k 
- +25% burst cushion (reserved hot buffer nodes across regions): monthly = $104.6k (+24%) 
- Option: Tri-region asymmetric commit (US 60%, EU 25%, APAC 15%) reduces blended run-rate by ~7% vs symmetric split.

Notes on HW choices: H100 gives best latency and NVL for large context; A100 is cost-effective for embeddings-heavy or high-batch throughput. If HelixAI expects >60% low-latency chat traffic in US, recommend shifting an additional 10–15% to H100s.

Action: I can produce a month-by-month ramp (M1–M6) with commit bands if procurement needs staged PO amounts. Laura — can you confirm whether Helix asked for monthly invoices or quarterly?

—Karthik
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@helixai.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2027 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tri-region onboarding — SOW revisions and next steps

Emma — thanks for the clear asks. I've updated the SOW with: node mix per region, 25% burst clause, compliance checklist for Frankfurt and a note about Singapore PDPA items (attached as HelixAI_SOW_v1.2.pdf). I also added a DocuSign envelope link for the initial M1–M3 commitment (https://docusign.com/doc/abc1234).

Quick summary of next steps: 
1) Procurement to confirm whether they want the asymmetric split Karthik suggested or the symmetric split in your sheet; include billing cadence preference (monthly vs quarterly).
2) Sign SOW/PO (DocuSign) — Laura to send final PO template after you confirm amounts.
3) Redwood to provision baseline Dedicated pools (US/EU/APAC) within 10 business days after PO + 24–48 hours to enable 25% burst buffer in region.

If procurement needs a short call to align invoice terms and lead times, I'm available tomorrow 09:00-12:00 PT.

—Laura
Senior Commercial Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
